item.title: CLOSING RECEPTION of VENUS VS PINK Exhibition presented by Susan N Stewart and Catharina Goldnau — Sat Oct 24, 1:00 PM — Dignam Gallery in the Women's Art Association of Canada
item.description:
VENUS VS PINK EXHIBITION
Two artists. Two very different worlds. One seriously colourful encounter.
Susan N Stewart brings the heat with bold, vibrant paintings that swing from pure joy and excitement to moments of unexpected calm and serenity.
Catharina Goldnau's VENUS sculptures are a different kind of force. Each figure is hand-crafted from custom clay, capturing a distinct emotional state — raw, imperfect, powerful, and unapologetically human. And holding it all together? A solid foundation of Canadian Shield rock.
Paint meets clay. Colour meets earth. Pink meets Venus.
Come see what happens when these worlds collide at the Dignam Gallery in the Women's Art Association of Canada! Talk to the incredible artists and enjoy the beautiful space with refreshments on Saturday October 24th, 2026 from 1-4PM.

item.title: Maxime Van de Moortel (University of Toronto, Maths Department) — Wed Oct 28, 1:49 PM — Idealab Bridge
item.description:
Title: The interior of dynamical black hole
Abstract: The celebrated singularity theorem of Penrose predicts the existence of an incomplete causal geodesic in the interior of a black hole; however, this situation is compatible with the absence of a curvature singularity, e.g., at the Cauchy horizon of a Kerr black hole.
The Strong Cosmic Censorship conjecture, on the other hand, claims the presence of a (curvature) singularity generically, which preserves the deterministic evolution of the Einstein equations: in particular, the Kerr Cauchy horizon is non-generic.
We'll review recent progress towards a proof of the conjecture and towards understanding gravitational collapse for rotating black holes in classical gravity. Host: Soumendra Kishore Roy
Source: CITA Seminars

item.title: Build a Cloud-Native Foundation for AI with Azure Red Hat OpenShift — Wed Oct 28, 2:00 PM
item.description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto What does it take to build a cloud-native platform foundation for modern applications and AI workloads?
Join us to explore Azure Red Hat OpenShift (ARO) and the role of open-source Kubernetes in your platform strategy. We’ll introduce ARO, explore hosted control planes, and discuss how OpenShift Virtualization brings virtual machines onto a cloud-native platform alongside containerized applications.
Along the way, we’ll examine ARO’s security posture and platform considerations for financial services and other highly regulated industries. Leave with a clearer understanding of ARO’s capabilities and how to evaluate it as part of your application modernization and AI infrastructure strategy.
Source: Meetup: Microsoft Reactor Toronto

### Haunted Hotels, Dark History & The Ghosts of Downtown
Toronto has a long history — and some of it is considerably darker than the history books make it sound.
Join us for an evening walk through **Old Toronto**, where we'll uncover stories of haunted hotels, gruesome executions, mysterious deaths, and some of the stranger legends that have become part of the city's history. We'll walk through the downtown core as the city settles into the evening, stopping along the way for stories about the ghosts, tragedies, and unusual events connected to the streets and buildings around us. And yes, we'll even explore **why Toronto has a long-standing fear of clowns.** 🤡👻
This isn't simply a walk through downtown. It's a **curated storytelling experience** that looks at some of Toronto's history from a decidedly darker perspective.

item.title: BOOK READING: THE SUN WILL SHINE ON MY TOMORROW, BY SANDEE MACGREGOR — Fri Oct 30, 6:30 PM — Blackhurst Cultural Centre
item.description:
📚☀️🌅The book "The Sun Will Shine on My Tomorrow,” by Sandee MacGregor, tells the true story of Dorice Lusuli, a young girl in Nairobi, Kenya, who lost both of her parents and was left facing fear, grief, and uncertainty about what would come next. Through the care of her grandmother and the support of a caring village, Baba Nyumbani, she found the food, school fees, and protection she needed, along with a renewed sense of hope for her future. Sandee Macgregor is a Canadian author based in Southern Ontario. Trained as a teacher, she is the author of two bestselling devotionals as well as two children’s books, "Lucy's Adoption Story" and "Can I Take It to Heaven?" Meet the author and learn about Dorice's story of resilience growing up as an orphan and about the organization that supported every step of the way. Free to attend. All are welcome! #ReadDifferently📚
Source: A Different Booklist
